title: Genotyping Before Treatment: HLA-B*57:01, DPYD and TPMT/NUDT15
summary: Use pre-treatment genotypes to prevent severe drug toxicity: avoid abacavir in HLA-B*57:01 carriers, and set or avoid fluoropyrimidine and thiopurine doses from DPYD and TPMT/NUDT15 metabolizer status (CPIC).

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 75 Hits 4, 5 and 11 and Traps 1 and 2 (first lesson for Ch. 75). Checked against Martin 2012 (CPIC abacavir; read via page fetch) and its 2014 update (abstract), Amstutz 2018 (CPIC DPYD) and Maillard 2026 (CPIC TPMT/NUDT15 2025 update). Updates: CPIC 2025 starts TPMT intermediate metabolizers at 30–80% of standard dose (reviewer: “reduce 35–50%”); TPMT *2, *3B, *3C account for > 90% of low activity (reviewer: *2, *3A, *3C > 95%). Not taught: “3–5% DPD deficient” and the “25–50%” intermediate reduction range, FDA labeling statements.

objectives: Distinguish immune-mediated (HLA) from metabolic (enzyme) pharmacogenomic risk.
Apply CPIC recommendations for HLA-B*57:01 and abacavir.
Apply DPYD and TPMT/NUDT15 metabolizer status to dosing.

scenes.title: Three genotypes that stop a prescription
scenes.altText: Three invented pre-treatment reports: (1) HIV patient about to start abacavir — HLA-B*57:01 positive; (2) colon cancer patient about to start 5-fluorouracil — DPYD c.1905+1G>A heterozygous; (3) child with acute lymphoblastic leukemia about to start mercaptopurine — TPMT two no-function alleles. Question token: “Give the standard dose, reduce it, or avoid the drug?”

cues.text: Three genotype reports arrive before treatment. An HIV patient due to start abacavir carries HLA-B star 57:01.
A colon cancer patient due to start 5-fluorouracil carries one copy of the DPYD variant c.1905+1G>A. And a child with leukemia due to start mercaptopurine has two non-functional TPMT alleles.
For each: standard dose, reduced dose, or avoid the drug?

scenes.title: Two kinds of risk gene
scenes.altText: Two branches. Immune-mediated: HLA-B presents peptides to immune cells; the HLA-B*57:01 allele is associated with abacavir hypersensitivity (Martin 2012). Metabolic: enzymes that inactivate a drug — DPD (gene DPYD) breaks down 5-fluorouracil; TPMT and NUDT15 catabolize thiopurines (mercaptopurine, azathioprine). Reduced or absent enzyme activity → drug or toxic metabolite accumulates at standard doses (Amstutz 2018; Maillard 2026).

cues.text: There are two kinds of risk gene here. The first is immune: HLA-B presents peptides to immune cells, and the HLA-B star 57:01 allele is linked to hypersensitivity to abacavir.
The second is metabolic: enzymes that inactivate a drug. DPD, encoded by DPYD, breaks down 5-fluorouracil.
TPMT and NUDT15 break down thiopurines such as mercaptopurine and azathioprine.
When those enzymes are reduced or absent, standard doses let the drug or its toxic products accumulate.

scenes.title: Abacavir and HLA-B*57:01
scenes.altText: Abacavir card (Martin 2012 CPIC): without genetic prescreening, ~5–8% of patients develop hypersensitivity during the first 6 weeks, and it can be life-threatening on repeated dosing. HLA-B*57:01 screening has a high negative predictive value (> 99%). In the PREDICT-1 trial, immunologically confirmed hypersensitivity occurred in 2.7% of 842 unscreened controls and in none of the screened-negative patients. Recommendation: HLA-B*57:01 positive → abacavir is not recommended; negative → standard dosing. The 2014 CPIC update found no evidence to change these recommendations.

cues.text: Without screening, about 5 to 8 percent of patients develop abacavir hypersensitivity in the first six weeks, and repeated dosing can be life-threatening.

Screening for HLA-B star 57:01 has a negative predictive value above 99 percent. In the PREDICT-1 trial, 2.7 percent of unscreened patients had confirmed hypersensitivity, versus none of those screened negative.
So: HLA-B star 57:01 positive, abacavir is not recommended. Negative, use standard dosing.
The 2014 update reviewed new evidence and left these recommendations unchanged.

scenes.title: DPYD and TPMT/NUDT15: dose by activity
scenes.altText: DPYD card (Amstutz 2018 CPIC): four key decreased/no-function variants — c.1905+1G>A (*2A), c.1679T>G (*13), c.2846A>T, c.1129–5923C>G (HapB3); ~7% of Europeans carry at least one. Activity score: two no-function = poor metabolizer (AS 0) → avoid 5-FU regimens; one decreased/no-function = intermediate (AS 1–1.5) → reduced starting dose (c.1905+1G>A carriers given 50% had toxicity comparable to non-carriers). TPMT/NUDT15 card (Maillard 2026 CPIC 2025): intermediate metabolizers → start at 30–80% of standard dose (if standard ≥ 75 mg/m²/day for malignancy); poor metabolizers → malignancy: reduce dose 10-fold, give 3 days/week; non-malignant conditions: alternative non-thiopurine; TPMT *2, *3B, *3C account for > 90% of low-activity phenotypes. Back to the hook: abacavir → avoid; 5-FU → reduced starting dose; mercaptopurine (ALL, TPMT poor metabolizer) → ~10-fold reduction, thrice weekly.

cues.text: For 5-fluorouracil, four DPYD variants matter most, and about 7 percent of Europeans carry at least one. Two non-functional variants make a poor metabolizer: avoid 5-fluorouracil regimens.
One decreased or non-functional variant makes an intermediate metabolizer: start at a reduced dose. Carriers of c.1905+1G>A given half the dose had toxicity rates like non-carriers.
For thiopurines, TPMT or NUDT15 intermediate metabolizers start at 30 to 80 percent of the standard dose.
Poor metabolizers with cancer get a tenfold lower dose, three days a week; for non-malignant disease, choose a non-thiopurine drug.
Back to the reports: abacavir, avoid. 5-fluorouracil, reduce the starting dose. Mercaptopurine in a TPMT poor metabolizer with leukemia, reduce about tenfold and give three times weekly.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “HLA-B*57:01-positive patients can take abacavir with close monitoring” (✓ not recommended — hypersensitivity can be life-threatening); “A DPYD poor metabolizer just needs a slightly lower 5-FU dose” (✓ avoid fluoropyrimidine regimens; intermediates get reduced starting doses); “TPMT matters only in Europeans” (✓ TPMT and NUDT15 variants occur in all populations; frequencies vary by ancestry).

cues.text: Trap one: an HLA-B star 57:01 carrier can take abacavir with close monitoring. No: abacavir is not recommended, because hypersensitivity can be life-threatening.
Trap two: a DPYD poor metabolizer just needs a slightly lower dose. No: avoid 5-fluorouracil regimens; dose reduction is for intermediate metabolizers.
Trap three: thiopurine genes matter only in one population. TPMT and NUDT15 variants occur in all world populations, with frequencies varying by ancestry.

scenes.title: Allergy gene says NO; enzyme gene says HOW MUCH
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “The immune gene says NO; the enzyme gene says HOW MUCH.” Tokens: HLA-B*57:01 → no abacavir · DPYD/TPMT intermediate → less · poor → avoid or drastically less. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the immune gene says no; the enzyme gene says how much. HLA-B star 57:01 means no abacavir. DPYD or TPMT intermediate metabolizers get less; poor metabolizers avoid the drug or get drastically less.

Where it breaks: TPMT poor metabolizers with cancer can still receive heavily reduced thiopurine; patients without risk variants can still have toxicity; and doses are adjusted afterwards by tolerance and monitoring.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “HLA-B*57:01 + → abacavir not recommended (HSR ~5–8% unscreened; NPV > 99%)”, “DPYD PM → avoid 5-FU, IM → reduced start · TPMT/NUDT15 IM → 30–80% start, PM → 10-fold ↓ (cancer) or alternative”.

cues.text: Pre-treatment genotyping prevents severe toxicity: HLA-B*57:01 carriers should not receive abacavir, while DPYD and TPMT/NUDT15 results set the starting dose or rule out fluoropyrimidines and thiopurines.

props.label: DPYD PM avoid / IM reduce · TPMT IM 30–80% · PM 10-fold ↓ or alternative

explanation.what: Plain language: some people carry gene versions that make a standard drug dose dangerous — either by triggering an immune reaction or by failing to break the drug down — so a genetic test before treatment tells the prescriber to avoid the drug or lower the dose. Scientific terms: HLA-B*57:01, hypersensitivity reaction (HSR), negative predictive value, dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD, DPYD), activity score, thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT), NUDT15, metabolizer phenotype, thioguanine nucleotides.
explanation.why: HLA-B presents peptides to immune cells, and the HLA-B*57:01 allele is associated with abacavir hypersensitivity. DPD inactivates 5-fluorouracil; TPMT and NUDT15 inactivate thiopurine metabolites; reduced activity raises exposure to active or toxic metabolites (e.g., excessive TGNs in TPMT-deficient patients) at standard doses.
explanation.measure: Abacavir: HSR ~5–8% in first 6 weeks without prescreening; NPV > 99%; PREDICT-1 2.7% of 842 unscreened vs none screened-negative; carriers → not recommended (Martin 2012). DPYD: four key variants; ~7% of Europeans carry ≥ 1; AS 0 → avoid; AS 1–1.5 → reduced starting dose; 50% reduction in c.1905+1G>A carriers gave toxicity comparable to non-carriers (Amstutz 2018). TPMT/NUDT15 (Maillard 2026): IM 30–80% of standard start; PM malignancy 10-fold reduction 3 days/week; PM non-malignancy alternative agent.
explanation.differs: Immune (HLA; avoid regardless of dose) vs metabolic (enzyme; dose proportional to activity); intermediate (reduce) vs poor (avoid or drastic reduction) metabolizers.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: HLA-B*57:01 and abacavir, DPYD poor vs intermediate metabolizer actions, and TPMT dosing.

mnemonic.explanation: HLA-B*57:01 → no abacavir; DPYD/TPMT/NUDT15 activity sets the dose (and DPYD poor metabolizers avoid 5-FU).
mnemonic.limitation: TPMT poor metabolizers with cancer receive heavily reduced thiopurine rather than none; non-carriers can still have toxicity; doses are titrated afterwards.

questions.stem: An HIV patient tests positive for HLA-B*57:01. What does CPIC recommend regarding abacavir?

options.rationale: Correct. Carriers are at high risk of potentially life-threatening hypersensitivity.
Incorrect. Hypersensitivity is immune-mediated; dose reduction does not make it safe.

options.text: Use abacavir with close monitoring for 6 weeks
options.rationale: Incorrect. The recommendation is not to prescribe abacavir.
Incorrect. Standard dosing is for non-carriers.

questions.stem: A patient carries two no-function DPYD variants (activity score 0). What is the recommendation for 5-fluorouracil?

options.rationale: Correct. DPYD poor metabolizers are at high risk of severe or fatal toxicity.
Incorrect. Modest reductions apply to intermediate metabolizers, not poor metabolizers.
Incorrect. Standard doses risk life-threatening toxicity.

options.text: Double the dose to overcome resistance
options.rationale: Incorrect. Low DPD activity increases exposure, not resistance.

questions.stem: A child with ALL is a TPMT intermediate metabolizer, with normal NUDT15. Per CPIC 2025, how should mercaptopurine be started (standard dose ≥ 75 mg/m²/day)?

options.text: At 30–80% of the standard starting dose
options.rationale: Correct. Intermediate metabolizers start at a reduced dose and are titrated by tolerance.
Incorrect. 30–60% of TPMT intermediate metabolizers cannot tolerate full doses.
Incorrect. That is for poor metabolizers with malignancy.
Incorrect. Alternatives are recommended for poor metabolizers with non-malignant conditions.
